newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Postal Service investigating "racist E-mail".
newsitem.headline: U.S. Postal Service investigating "racist E-mail".

text.p: The U.S. Postal Service Monday condemned a racist electronic message reportedly distributed by a postal employee and said it was investigating the incident.

The American Postal Workers Union had released a copy of the electronic mail message Monday, along with a letter to Postmaster General Marvin Runyon, calling it a "a vicious, racist message covered with black humour."

The message was transmitted by Walter Pavlik, a high-ranking New York-based manager of the postal system, "utilizing postal technology on postal time," union executive vice president William Burrus said in the letter.

The E-mail message, entitled "Ebonics Made Easy", used racial slurs and a grossly distorted interpretation of Black English to poke fun at an Oakland city schools programme to include the dialect spoken by some African-American.

"The Postal Service obviously does not condone any actions by an employee which are racist in nature," Postal Service national spokesman Roy Betts said in a statement. "We find the content of this message to be repugnant and highly offensive."
The Postal Inspection Service was investigating the incident, Betts said.
"Swift and appropriate action will be taken if any employee is involved with the distribution of this racist statement," he said.

The postal workers union drew parallels between the incident and recent class action law suits against Texaco, Denny's and Mitsubishi Motors. Those cases, it said, "revealed that racism flourishes when there is not direct intervention at the highest levels of management with a message that it is unacceptable."
The language of the electronic message contained "obnoxious humour (which) clearly falls within the parameter of a threat to the respect and dignity of workers of colour," Burrus said.
